repo_notes.content: Audience and voice: this wiki serves two readers, in this order — (1) the maintainer (Calvin) returning after months away, who needs invariants, gotchas, why-decisions, and where-to-change-what fast; (2) recruiters and peer engineers evaluating the engineering practice (zero-JS architecture, test-gated deploys, CSS-only animation). Always prefer explaining WHY a decision was made and WHAT breaks if violated — and which test or comment guards it — over restating what the code does: the 'what' is a handful of small .astro files anyone can read in minutes. The primary sources are the in-repo why-comments (the .github/workflows/ci.yml header, the index.astro grid comment, the uno.config.ts safelist and inline-block comments, test-file doc blocks) — quote them with line anchors rather than paraphrasing.

Architecture ground truth (treat contradictions as errors): the production site is fully static — astro.config.mjs sets output: 'static'; no adapter, no server runtime, no middleware. dist/_astro contains zero .js files and no serverless/edge function is emitted — enforced by the literal test names 'ships zero external JavaScript files' and 'emits no server runtime for any host' in tests/build-output.test.ts. It contains TWO CSS chunks, not one: Vite splits per entry and this site has had a second route since /patches shipped. Any claim of a single stylesheet is stale, and so is the test name 'emits exactly one stylesheet', which no longer exists — Astro's inlineStylesheets:'auto' also moves a small sheet into the page, so 'what CSS does this page load' is answered by pageCss() in tests/helpers/css.ts and never by reading dist/_astro. The page ships zero <svg>: every icon is a UnoCSS presetIcons CSS mask rule. Total first-party client JS is two tiny inline scripts: the pre-paint theme resolver in src/layouts/BasicLayout.astro and ThemeSwitcher's toggle listener. The only external script is third-party Umami analytics, whose tag is emitted unconditionally — the UMAMI_ID env var only populates its data-website-id attribute; do not describe the script as conditionally rendered. Svelte, the motion library, the @astrojs/netlify SSR adapter, and astro-icon were all deliberately DELETED in past improvement runs — treat any trace as historical, never document them as present.

Upstream-contamination warning: this repo is a fork of Ladvace/astro-bento-portfolio that has diverged substantially, and prior auto-generated docs blended upstream and pre-refactor knowledge into descriptions of this repo. Specifically: Card (src/components/Card/index.astro) has ONLY the props {title?, titleIcon?, colSpan?, rowSpan?, fillsArea?} — no href mode, no arrow-up hover, no colorText/height/padding/bgColor (features of the deleted pre-refactor Card). ProgressBar.astro contains ZERO JavaScript — no IntersectionObserver, no scroll-triggered animation anywhere in current source (the term survives only in archived plans/done/ documents describing the deleted Svelte component); it animates with a pure-CSS progress-grow keyframe on page load. The fork's whole identity is having deleted that JavaScript — re-derive every claim about interactivity from current source.

Content-pipeline facts every page must get right: src/lib/constants.ts is the single source of every user-facing string; its exports are LINKS, CAREER, ABOUT_ME, GOALS (plural — a Goal[] array; there is NO singular GOAL export), WELCOME, NOW, FOOTER, METADATA, GOAL_YEAR, EVENTS, PATCHES, NEXT_RACE, THEME_TOGGLE, the helpers stravaActivityUrl/clampToGoal/goalForSport, and the types Goal/Sport/RaceEvent. The Goal type's progress_last_year is number|null, and NOTHING RENDERS IT — the goal card's "last year's" line was removed to pay for the next-race countdown, so do not describe it as displaying a dash or anything else; it is configured, unrendered, and one edit from returning. Icons stored in constants are Iconify ids ('collection:name') converted to UnoCSS classes solely by iconClass() in src/lib/icons.ts — the one mapping components and the uno.config.ts safelist must share; the single exception is ThemeSwitcher's sun/moon icons, literal i-ri-* classes written in the component source that UnoCSS extracts directly and that never touch iconClass() or the safelist. METADATA.email_obfuscated is defined and test-gated but never rendered by any component — do not list it as page content.

Settled decisions — present as decisions with their recorded rationale, never as gaps, bugs, or TODOs for the reader: GitHub Actions IS the CI and Cloudflare Pages is the host — plan 019 moved the build off Netlify and the Netlify project has since been DELETED, so the run-1 DX-01 rejection ('GitHub Actions was offered and declined') is history and must never be presented as current policy; the deploy jobs deliberately have no checkout, so no repository source runs in a runner holding the deploy token; constants.ts sits outside the eslint glob (test-gated instead); @typescript-eslint/parser looks unused but is resolved at runtime by eslint-plugin-astro — removing it breaks linting; no Playwright (deliberate for two lines of client JS); og:url and canonical are BOTH `Astro.url.href` and therefore agree exactly — BasicLayout.astro says so in a comment; the note that used to sit here claimed og:url was origin-only by design and instructed the reader never to describe them as equal, which was the inverse of the truth and would have had a generator write a falsehood; robots.txt and llms.txt are GENERATED endpoints (src/pages/robots.txt.ts and src/pages/llms.txt.ts) that derive their identity from constants.ts — PR #108 replaced the hand-written files in public/, so there is no manual-sync obligation left to describe; the sitemap deliberately carries NO lastmod, because every input this repo has for one was measured wrong in both directions; the maintainer's self-description copy is deliberately left to him. NOTE: the Strava progress automation SHIPPED in plan 015 — `.github/workflows/strava-progress.yml` rewrites `src/data/strava-progress.json` nightly, so `current_progress` is bot-owned and must not be described as hand-edited.

plans/ is a decision ledger, not source code. plans/README.md is the living index; its execution table with per-plan commit hashes is the AUTHORITATIVE status source — its prose header has demonstrably lagged its own table (the header said plans 011–014 were TODO after the table marked 011 DONE). Read statuses from the table at generation time: never present a TODO plan as shipped, never document an archived plan's pre-change description as current architecture, and take the next plan number from the index (numbering is monotonic across runs). plans/done/README.md archives per-plan verification evidence (mutation-tested assertions, preview-vs-production diffs). Rejected findings are recorded WITH refutation evidence precisely so they are never re-derived.

Currency rule: derive every quantitative claim — test/assertion counts, dependency counts, component counts, the number of improvement runs, goal km figures, byte sizes, plan statuses, commit hashes, the stagger-ladder length vs <main> child count — from the current code at generation time, never from README, memory, or plans prose. This repository is a continuous work in progress: page titles deliberately avoid frozen counts, and generated prose must never introduce one that will rot. This repo has documented history of numbers rotting in prose: a 3000km-vs-5000km description drift shipped to production (which is why constants.test.ts now forces METADATA.description to mention each goal's target figure), and the improve-run prompts carried stale numbers twice. Anchor each claim to the file and lines it comes from.

Scope and skip list: ignore dist/, node_modules/, .netlify/, .scratchpad/, .claude/, .husky internals beyond the one-line pre-commit, and pnpm-lock.yaml. README.md owns getting-started/quickstart — link to it, never duplicate a second setup guide. CLAUDE.md is agent instructions, not human documentation subject matter. llms.txt and robots.txt are build outputs of src/pages/llms.txt.ts and src/pages/robots.txt.ts — describe the derivation, never the emitted text, and do not build pages from their content. public/ now holds only _headers, favicon.ico, preview.jpg and resume.pdf. This is a small site — a bento-grid home page plus a patch wall at /patches with one prerendered page per sport (count routes and source files at generation time if a figure is needed): generate EXACTLY the specified pages — no per-component pages, no glossary, no contributing/roadmap/FAQ boilerplate. Package management is pnpm only (packageManager is pinned; npm install ignores pnpm-lock.yaml).

pages.title: Overview: A Zero-JavaScript Portfolio
pages.purpose: Orient both audiences in one read: calvin.sg is a bento-grid portfolio built on Astro + UnoCSS — a single-screen home page plus /patches, a wall of every race the owner has entered in any year drawn as bibs, prerendered per sport with output: 'static', no adapter, and no client framework, deployed to Cloudflare Pages by GitHub Actions. Frame the engineering identity as subtraction, and lead with the thesis that each removal is 'locked, not just done' — enforced by an assertion, not asserted in prose. Present the headline decisions as a compact before/after table: fully static output replacing an SSR build that served the page from a 2.4MB Netlify function (plan 002, commit 32071fe); zero external JavaScript files replacing a Svelte+motion client runtime (plan 003, commit 621dd5a); zero <svg> — icons are CSS mask rules (plan 006; locked indirectly by build-output.test.ts's per-icon mask-rule assertions — there is no explicit no-<svg> test, so do not claim one); CSS-only animation; a deploy gated by the test suite itself (.github/workflows/ci.yml: the build job runs 'pnpm check', 'pnpm eslint' and 'pnpm test', and both deploy jobs sit behind 'needs: build'). These change-commit hashes were verified in git history at authoring time and history does not rot — do not reconcile them against the plans/README.md execution table, which records completion status and whose per-plan hash can be a different commit. Cite 'ships zero external JavaScript files' and 'emits no server runtime for any host' as literal test names in tests/build-output.test.ts. Enumerate what client code remains: the pre-paint theme script in src/layouts/BasicLayout.astro, ThemeSwitcher's toggle listener, and the always-emitted Umami analytics tag. Note the fork lineage (Ladvace/astro-bento-portfolio, substantially diverged). Include one mermaid diagram of the system: src/lib/constants.ts → the constants-consuming components (derive the exact list from src/components imports at generation time — not every component consumes constants) → prerendered dist/ → test suites → the uploaded artifact → Cloudflare Pages. Close with a documentation map — README.md owns setup (link, don't restate), plans/ is the decision ledger (see this wiki's Engineering Log page), and this wiki's Maintainer Playbook page is the first stop after time away.

page_notes.content: Keep this page short and diagram-led — it is the recruiter landing page. The removed stack (Svelte, motion, SSR adapter, astro-icon) appears only as the 'before' column with plans/ citations, never in present tense. 'Engineering Log' and 'Maintainer Playbook' are cross-references to sibling pages of this wiki, not repository files.

pages.title: Maintainer Playbook: Invariants and Change Recipes
pages.purpose: The page future-Calvin opens after six months away. Structure as task-oriented recipes, each naming the exact files and the trap that fires, cross-linking the system pages for mechanism detail: (1) Bump goal progress — edit GOALS[n].current_progress in src/lib/constants.ts; constants.test.ts enforces progress finite and within [0, total_goal], and METADATA.description must mention each goal's target figure (the drift gate added after a 3000km-vs-5000km description drift shipped). (2) Add or remove a card — the lg grid packs completely full (quote the current index.astro inline comment for the exact cell arithmetic at generation time; bug history in PR #42): re-balance lg row/col spans in IntroCard/AboutMe/Now, AND extend the nth-child stagger ladder in BasicLayout.astro — a lockstep test in build-output.test.ts pins the ladder to the card count (plan 013), so a missing rung fails the deploy. (3) Add a social link — append to LINKS; its icon is auto-safelisted because uno.config.ts maps over LINKS; but an icon in a NEW constants field silently renders as nothing until the safelist maps over that field too. (4) Change job/role — CAREER[0].job_name is the site's only record of the current job and five surfaces derive from it: JSON-LD worksFor/jobTitle in BasicLayout, the llms.txt blockquote and career line (PR #108), the intro card h1, and METADATA.title (which also feeds og:title/twitter:title). Nothing is hand-typed any more — two stale copies shipped before they were derived — but the title has a measured width budget, so a LONGER job title can red tests/constants.test.ts; that gate is working, and the note on METADATA.title says what to do. (5) Iterate on tests — SKIP_BUILD=1 pnpm test reuses dist/. Then a hard 'do not helpfully fix' list with evidence links: the deploy jobs' missing checkout (deliberate — see the Deploy Pipeline page); @typescript-eslint/parser (runtime-resolved by eslint-plugin-astro — removal breaks linting, refuted in plans/README.md); constants.ts outside the eslint glob (test-gated instead); og:url and canonical both resolve to Astro.url.href and agree (an earlier revision of this file asserted the opposite); monotonic plan numbering (read the next number from plans/README.md); pnpm only, never npm.

page_notes.content: Recipes intentionally restate invariants owned by system pages, but as one-line trap + link, not full mechanism. Verify each recipe's file references against current source at generation time.

pages.title: Architecture: The Bento Grid and the Patch Wall
pages.purpose: Document the full render path and component contracts. src/layouts/BasicLayout.astro wraps every page — src/pages/index.astro (the bento grid) and src/pages/patches/[...sport].astro (one rest-parameter route prerendering /patches, /patches/cycling and /patches/running) — and builds the entire <head> from constants: OG/Twitter tags, canonical, a JSON-LD Person schema (sameAs filtered to absolute LINKS URLs, worksFor/jobTitle from CAREER[0]), and the deferred Umami script tag — emitted unconditionally, with the UMAMI_ID env var populating only its data-website-id attribute. It also carries the load-bearing inline <script is:inline> that resolves theme from localStorage/prefers-color-scheme and stamps <html data-theme> before first paint, while the static markup hard-codes data-theme="light" so a no-JS visitor gets the full designed palette instead of transparent cards (colors are CSS custom properties scoped to :root[data-theme]). The bento grid: md 2-col; lg 4-col × 8-row with a height budget that is a FLOOR AND NO CEILING — `lg:min-h-[clamp(46rem,100vh,50rem)]` — and rows sized to their content (`min-content`, not eight fractions). Both are required by WCAG SC 1.4.12: a reader may enlarge the type without moving any font-size the page can see, so a grid that cannot grow deletes the difference (1157.7px measured at 1024x600 before the fix). The rem spelling additionally lets the budget grow under text zoom; every breakpoint is likewise rem (uno.config.ts theme.breakpoints restates presetWind3's defaults as 40/48/64/80/96rem), and tests/page-fit.test.ts forbids an absolute length in either place; quote the index.astro inline comment verbatim and re-read it at generation time, because the packing arithmetic changes whenever cards change — at authoring time the lg grid was packed exactly 32/32 cells, and adding a card without re-balancing lg spans in IntroCard/AboutMe/Now lets auto-placement push the Now card into a zero-height implicit row and clip it (shipped as a real bug, fixed in PR #42). Give a compact component roster table derived from src/components at generation time, not subpages; contracts verified at authoring time include: Card is the only primitive with props {title?, titleIcon?, colSpan?, rowSpan?, fillsArea?} plus one named slot, `corner`, for marks that belong to the card rather than to a line of its copy — the Now card's live dot and its explainer link use it, and it is what let Now stop hand-rolling its own heading (which is why all six card headings now reserve the same space beneath them, not five); Goal renders generically from the Goal type (generalized in PR #41 for cycling + running); ProgressBar carries a full ARIA progressbar contract — aria-valuemax is the real km target, not 100, and aria-valuetext composes human-readable figures; IntroCard renders the portrait via astro:assets Image with densities=[2]; ThemeSwitcher is the ONLY interactive component. Icons are aria-hidden throughout, with sr-only companion text wherever an icon is the sole content, plus one further use that is not icon completion — NEW_TAB_NOTICE, on exactly the two links that open a new tab, one of which carries ~90 characters of visible text (the footer 'love' span, LINKS/Strava buttons, ThemeSwitcher's state-independent name from THEME_TOGGLE, and the Now card's corner explainer link, whose accessible name OPENS with NOW.explainer_name and ends with NEW_TAB_NOTICE); icon-beside-visible-text spots (Card's titleIcon, IntroCard's greeting, ProgressBar's goal icons) deliberately carry no sr-only twin. State explicitly: no scroll-triggered animation and no IntersectionObserver anywhere in current source — the term survives only in archived plans/done/ documents describing deleted code.

page_notes.content: Verify every prop and ARIA claim against current source — this repo's own pre-refactor Card had href/colorText/bgColor props, and its deleted Svelte ProgressBar (removed in plan 003) used an IntersectionObserver; neither exists in the current fork and prior auto-generated docs described both as present.

pages.title: Content as Typed Data: constants.ts
pages.purpose: Explain the repo's core pattern: src/lib/constants.ts as a typed, test-gated CMS. Walk each export and its consumers: LINKS (social buttons incl. /resume.pdf, JSON-LD sameAs), CAREER (Career card + JSON-LD worksFor/jobTitle), ABOUT_ME, GOALS (Goal[] — cover the type, especially progress_last_year: number|null where null means 'no comparable figure' — NOTHING RENDERS IT, the goal card's "last year's" line was removed to pay for the next-race countdown, so do not describe it as rendering a dash or anything else), WELCOME, NOW, FOOTER, METADATA (title/description/site_url/preview image/locality; note email_obfuscated is defined and test-gated but never rendered — intentional, see the rejected finding in plans/README.md). Explain src/lib/icons.ts: iconClass() maps 'collection:name' Iconify ids to UnoCSS classes, and BOTH components and the uno.config.ts safelist must go through it. The page's story is the gating decision: constants.ts sits outside the eslint glob BY DESIGN, and tests/constants.test.ts is its validator — installed icon collections only (fa6-brands, ri), finite goal numerics within [0, total_goal], absolute vs root-relative URL shapes, SEO title/description length bounds, and the flagship drift gate requiring METADATA.description to mention each goal's target figure (a 3000km-vs-5000km drift shipped once — that is the why). Diagram the flow: constants.ts → components, forking into the in-process Container render asserted by tests/rendered-html.test.ts and the prerendered dist/ asserted by tests/build-output.test.ts. Derive which exports rendered-html.test.ts actually asserts from its imports and assertions at generation time — never assume full coverage or a specific gap (a NOW/Career-dates gap existed until plan 014 closed it). Close with the referenced static assets: src/assets/me.webp (portrait, emitted at 1x/2x), public/resume.pdf, public/preview.jpg (og:image/twitter:image), favicon.ico, and public/_headers (the immutable cache rule for /_astro/, copied verbatim into dist/). llms.txt is NOT among them any more — it is generated by src/pages/llms.txt.ts from these same constants.

page_notes.content: The export is GOALS (plural array) — a previous config repeatedly said 'GOAL', a nonexistent symbol. Read current goal figures from the file at generation time; never freeze km numbers into prose.

pages.title: Styling, Theming, and the Icon Pipeline
pages.purpose: Document the coupled UnoCSS systems whose failure modes are silent. Icons: presetIcons turns @iconify-json/fa6-brands and @iconify-json/ri ids into CSS mask rules — zero <svg>, zero icon fonts. Quote the two load-bearing uno.config.ts comments: (1) icon classes are derived from constants at render time so UnoCSS never sees them literally — the safelist maps every configured icon id through iconClass(), enumerating the mapped constants.ts fields from uno.config.ts at generation time rather than from a frozen list.greeting_icon, and FOOTER.icon via the shared iconClass() helper; any icon class derived from constants that the safelist does not cover gets no CSS rule and renders as nothing, silently (the one exception: ThemeSwitcher's sun/moon icons are literal classes in component source, extracted by UnoCSS directly, needing no safelist); (2) presetIcons({scale: 1, extraProperties: {display: 'inline-block'}}) — without inline-block the icon <span> stays an inline box, width/height are ignored, and every icon renders at zero size. Diagram the coupling: constants.ts → iconClass() → {components, safelist} → build-output.test.ts asserting every safelisted class emits a rule with both a mask url and inline-block. Theming: color tokens are CSS custom properties under :root[data-theme='light'|'dark'] in BasicLayout — NOT UnoCSS theme tokens (uno.config.ts DOES declare a `theme` block, but it holds only the five breakpoints restated in rem — no colour or shadow token lives there. `boxShadow.custom` is gone because the offset plate is now written as ONE complete arbitrary value, `shadow-[2px_2px_0_var(--shadow)]`, in the single `control` shortcut — split across a geometry utility and a colour-only one it left `--un-shadow-color` undefined and computed to none. `colors.gray.300` is gone because ProgressBar's track now takes `--progress-track`, just as its fill took `--progress-fill` in place of the borrowed `--shadow`). Walk the flash-free flow: pre-paint script stamps data-theme → variables switch → ThemeSwitcher toggles and persists to localStorage, with its sun/moon icons selected purely in CSS via a descendant selector that deliberately outranks presetIcons' display rule (quoted comment in ThemeSwitcher.astro). Then the full CSS-only motion inventory: the card-in entrance keyframe with the hand-enumerated nth-child 0.08s stagger ladder over <main>'s children (check the ladder against the rendered card count at generation time — GOALS.map in index.astro and CAREER.map in Career.astro each emit one card per entry, so count entries, not JSX children; a lockstep test in build-output.test.ts pins ladder coverage to the card count since plan 013), ProgressBar's progress-grow keyframe (1.5s ease-in-out, 0.3s delay, backwards fill) growing to a --progress inline custom property, and Pulse's animate-ping — all load-time. card-in and progress-grow carry prefers-reduced-motion opt-outs; Pulse's animate-ping is the stock presetWind3 utility with NO reduced-motion gate — report it as the one un-gated animation, do not paper over it. Note the second silent-failure class: UnoCSS generates nothing for typo utilities with no warning — enumerate the reintroduction gates from build-output.test.ts at generation time — at authoring time, the DEAD_CLASSES source scan plus the plan-012 gate requiring every class token in the shipped HTML to have a stylesheet rule.

page_notes.content: This page owns the icon-safelist and animation invariants; the Maintainer Playbook links here from its recipes. Anchor every claim to lines in uno.config.ts, src/lib/icons.ts, BasicLayout.astro, ThemeSwitcher.astro, ProgressBar.astro, Pulse.astro, or tests/build-output.test.ts (the safelist mask/inline-block assertions and the DEAD_CLASSES gate).

pages.title: Test Harness: A Green Build Is Not Evidence
pages.purpose: The strongest showcase page, framed by the doc-block principle from tests/build-output.test.ts: assert on rendered HTML and real dist/ artifacts, never on exit codes. Cover each vitest suite under tests/ and what it uniquely proves — enumerate the suites at generation time rather than assuming their number; those present at authoring time were: tests/rendered-html.test.ts renders index.astro in-process via Astro's experimental Container API, parses with linkedom, and asserts the constants reach the page — derive the asserted export set from the suite's imports at generation time (plan 014 closed the former NOW/Career-dates gap) — plus JSON-LD shape, the ARIA progressbar contract, aria-label/sr-only consistency, and icon reference counts. tests/constants.test.ts gates the data layer (see the Content page — it is constants.ts's ONLY validator). tests/build-output.test.ts opens real dist/ files: zero external JS (there are TWO CSS chunks since /patches added a second entry, and no assertion counts stylesheets any more), no SSR function output, the unicode-range emoji gate locking plan 011's migration (PR #108 widened it to scan dist/llms.txt and dist/robots.txt, which it used to skip on a reason that was false), a mask-url + inline-block rule for every safelisted icon class, the DEAD_CLASSES source gate, the class-to-rule pairing and stagger-lockstep gates from plans 012–013, and the sharpest assertion — a sharp-based pixel decode proving the portrait's 2x srcset candidate carries exactly twice the layout width, because Astro silently DROPS densities that would upscale and only decoding pixels catches the regression (originated from a real production PageSpeed finding). Surface the mutation-testing lessons recorded as comments IN the tests: icon references are counted rather than distinct classes because deleting one class kept the per-class version green; goal figures are matched as composed phrases because bare numbers also appear in prose. Harness mechanics for the returning maintainer: tests/setup/build.ts globalSetup runs one build (SKIP_BUILD=1 reuses dist/) and clears stale .netlify/ SSR output first — quote its in-file comment VERBATIM rather than paraphrasing; its point is that 'this build emitted no server runtime' is only meaningful about the current build, and a checkout that ever built with the old SSR adapter would otherwise keep that directory forever, failing locally while passing in CI; vitest.config.ts uses getViteConfig from astro/config and must keep unocss packages in server.deps.inline or the Container render breaks; and the linkedom quirk — dist/index.html's hoisted <script> above <html> leaves document.body empty, so assert text via string toContain and elements via querySelector. og:url and canonical are both Astro.url.href and are equal; do not repeat the retired warning that they differ by design.

page_notes.content: Do not hardcode assertion counts — read them from the suites at generation time. Quote real test names and in-file comments with line links; they are better documentation than any paraphrase and the credibility anchors for the recruiter audience.

pages.title: Deploy Pipeline: Actions Builds It, Cloudflare Pages Serves It
pages.purpose: Explain the pipeline that ships the site, and be exact about what orders it. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is the site's only builder and Cloudflare Pages serves only what that workflow uploads. The repository moved off Netlify in plan 019 and the Netlify project has since been DELETED — treat every surviving mention of netlify.toml, a Netlify build command, or a Netlify dashboard setting as comparative history, never as current configuration, and never tell a reader to check a Netlify dashboard. Diagram the job graph: one `build` job runs pnpm check, pnpm eslint and pnpm test (vitest's globalSetup runs astro build, so the suite asserts against the real dist/), then uploads that dist/ as an artifact; two deploy jobs — deploy-preview for same-repo pull requests, deploy-production for a push or workflow_dispatch on main — download the SAME artifact and publish it with `wrangler pages deploy`. NEITHER DEPLOY JOB REBUILDS, which is the point: what ships is byte-for-byte what the suite gated. The safety property is the `needs: build` edge. On Netlify 'a red suite cannot deploy' was a platform guarantee, because the build command WAS the suite; here it is one edge in a job graph that a refactor can drop while every check stays green. That is why tests/workflow-guards.test.ts exists — it reads the real workflow and EXECUTES the `if:` guards in GitHub's own expression evaluator (@actions/expressions) against a table of event contexts — read the table rather than quoting its length — because a guard that reads sensibly can still evaluate false on a payload where the referenced object is absent, and a skipped job renders as a grey check that reads as a pass. That defect shipped once. Cover the deliberate asymmetries a reader would otherwise 'fix': the deploy jobs have NO checkout, so no repository source runs in a runner holding the deploy token — which is also why they hardcode node-version instead of reading .nvmrc, an agreement the same test file now asserts across every workflow; CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN exists ONLY as an environment secret, which is what keeps the production environment's main-only branch policy meaningful; CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and UMAMI_ID are repository VARIABLES rather than secrets, by the project's own test — does the value ship publicly? — and marking either one secret would mask it in unrelated log lines while protecting nothing. Explain the artifact-age gate both deploy jobs carry: the build stamps the Singapore calendar day into every page, and GitHub's 'Re-run failed jobs' does not re-run `build`, so a deploy re-run the next morning would republish yesterday's countdowns and bibs; the step refuses an artifact whose stamp is not today. Netlify could not hit this, because its retry re-ran the build command. Note the second workflow, .github/workflows/strava-progress.yml: it is the nightly Strava fetch AND the site's only unattended deploy — a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no workflow run, so it dispatches ci.yml itself, unconditionally, because the site has a clock as well as a distance and every calendar page turns over at Singapore midnight whether or not the owner trained. Local gates: .husky/pre-commit runs lint-staged (eslint --fix on src/**/*.{js,astro}); flat eslint.config.js with eslint-plugin-astro + jsx-a11y recommended sets; tsconfig extends astro/tsconfigs/strict and its **/* include sweeps the root configs in, so pnpm check covers them. Also own the crawler surface: @astrojs/sitemap derives its URLs from astro.config.mjs's site value and deliberately emits NO lastmod — every input this repo has for one was measured wrong in BOTH directions, and the reasoning is recorded in the config — while robots.txt and llms.txt are generated endpoints under src/pages/ that derive their identity from constants.ts, and build-output.test.ts is what keeps astro.config's site coupled to METADATA.site_url. Close with the parity property: static output with no adapter means pnpm preview serves a dist/ byte-identical to production.

page_notes.content: Never recommend a second CI system, a build step inside a deploy job, or a gating check that runs against a deployed preview URL — the last one cannot be ordered, because the URL does not exist until the deploy it would gate has already happened. Every blocking check belongs in `build`, against the artifact; anything needing a live URL is reporting, not gating. And do not present Netlify as current infrastructure: the project was deleted after the plan 019 cutover, so the only correct tense for it is the past.

pages.title: Engineering Log: The plans/ Decision Ledger
pages.purpose: The single history page: summarize plans/ as the repo's decision ledger and a working example of governed agentic maintenance, so every other page describes only current state. This page must stay evergreen — the ledger grows run by run, so derive the plan list, per-plan statuses, and completion hashes from the plans/README.md execution table at generation time (authoritative for status; its own prose header has demonstrably lagged it before), and derive the run count and run grouping from the dated per-run headings in the index's 'Findings considered and rejected' section and each plan file's 'Planned at' line — the execution table itself carries no run column. Pull per-plan verification evidence from plans/done/README.md. Structure the narrative as: (1) the arc so far, grouped by run — milestones already in the ledger worth surfacing if still accurate include the regression safety net landing before any refactor, prerendering to static output and deleting the SSR adapter (before which the page lived inside a 2.4MB serverless function), deleting the Svelte+motion client runtime in favor of CSS, replacing astro-icon with presetIcons CSS masks, and the emoji-to-icon migration locked by the emoji-output gate — but always re-verify each against the table and never present this list as exhaustive or current; (2) the governance mechanics, with equal weight, because they are standing policy rather than history and the real differentiator: findings killed by a per-finding adversarial skeptic pass are recorded WITH refutation evidence so no future run re-derives them (examples recorded in the index: removing @typescript-eslint/parser would break linting since eslint-plugin-astro resolves it at runtime; 'add GitHub Actions CI' was maintainer-declined and its own cited evidence showed the deploy failing safely; Playwright judged disproportionate for the amount of client JS involved); the 'Deliberately not planned' section records the maintainer's explicit calls, not oversights — enumerate its current items from the index rather than assuming a count, and re-read them against the code: the llms.txt hand-sync obligation the index used to record was retired by PR #108, which turned that file into a generated endpoint; numbering is monotonic across runs, with the next plan number read from the index; the verified-baseline table must be re-checked each run because 'Every failure in the last run came from a plan believing something about the repo that had stopped being true' (quote it exactly, including 'about the repo'); and done/README.md's done-bar is mutation-tested assertions plus preview-vs-production byte diffs. Present all of it as decisions, never as defects or TODOs for the reader.

page_notes.content: Statuses, completion hashes, and the next plan number are volatile — read them from the plans/README.md execution table at generation time; the run count and grouping come from the index's dated run headings and the plan files' 'Planned at' lines, not the table. Never cap the narrative at a fixed number of runs, never present a TODO plan as shipped, and never describe pre-change architecture from archived plans as current.
